'''Detlef Gromoll''' (13 May 1938 – 31 May 2008) was a mathematician who worked in [[differential geometry]].

==Biography==

Gromoll was born in [[Berlin]] in 1938,<ref name="nytobit">{{cite news |first= Kenneth|last= Chang|authorlink= |title=Detlef Gromoll, Known for Math 'Soul' Idea, Dies at 70 |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/19/science/19gromoll.html |quote=Detlef Gromoll, a mathematician who helped lay the foundations for studying the abstract distortions of shapes in three or more dimensions, died on May 31 in Stony Brook, N.Y. He was 70. |work=[[New York Times]] |date= 2008-06-19|accessdate=2024-10-10 }}</ref> and was a classically trained violinist. 
After living and attending school in [[Rosdorf]] and graduating from high school in [[Bonn]], he obtained his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics at the [[University of Bonn]] in 1964.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9747}}</ref> 
Following sojourns at several universities, he joined the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]] in 1969.

He married Suzan L. Lemay on 29 December 1971, and they had three children together: Hans Christian (also a mathematician), Heidi, and Stefan, a physicist and cofounder of Scientific Media.<ref name="nytobit"/> He died in 2008 at age 70.
